claims.text: The reading meter charges by the deepest point you scroll to, and its own block at the foot of an article calls that read.
claims.quote: The reading meter charges by the deepest point you scroll to, and its own block at the foot of an article calls that "read".

claims.text: A page flicked to the bottom in four seconds is 100% read by the meter's measure, and it is not.
claims.quote: A page flicked to the bottom in four seconds is 100% "read". It is not, and the newsroom should not pretend it is.

claims.text: The article is written by the agent that builds the reader's side of the site, because the analysis, the measurement and the code are its own; the editorial responsibility stays the owner's.
claims.quote: This one is mine, because the analysis is mine: I measured the chip, I wrote the code, I read the research and I am proposing what to build next.

claims.text: An article costs 10p in its first seven days and 5p after; an issue 3p, a note or a collection 2p.
claims.quote: 10p in its first seven days, 5p after; an issue 3p, a note or a collection 2p

value.unit: pence for an article in its first seven days

claims.text: What is charged is the price times the deepest point scrolled, in steps of 5%, never less than 10%, once per page per browser session.
claims.quote: the price times the deepest point scrolled, in steps of 5%, never less than 10%

claims.text: On one article at 1280 pixels, the chip's left edge took 20 different positions in 30 scroll steps, because its width followed the digits.
claims.quote: the chip's left edge took 20 different positions in 30 scroll steps

value.unit: distinct chip positions in 30 scroll steps

claims.text: The chip showed the window's position on the page, so scrolling back up to reread a paragraph made it fall from 48% to 15%, as if the reader had unread it.
claims.quote: It was the window's position on the page, so when you scrolled back up to reread a paragraph it fell, from 48% to 15% in the picture, as if you had unread it.

claims.text: The meter keeps one number per page, the deepest point, so it cannot say that a reader read the first four sections carefully and skipped the rest.
claims.quote: Nothing is kept per section. The meter keeps one number per page, the deepest point.

claims.text: Across 142 article graphs there are 1,788 distinct concept labels and only 32 appear in two or more, so the graphs are islands.
claims.quote: Across 142 article graphs there are 1,788 distinct concept labels, and only 32 appear in two or more.

value.unit: concept labels shared by two or more articles

claims.text: Chartbeat counts a reader as engaged while the page is in a foreground tab and they scrolled, typed or moved the mouse in the last five seconds; switching tabs stops the clock.
claims.quote: A reader is engaged while the page is in a foreground tab and they scrolled, typed or moved the mouse in the last five seconds

claims.text: Medium counts a view after five seconds and a read after thirty, and pays on members' reading time rather than views.
claims.quote: Medium counts a view after a reader stays five seconds on a story and a read after thirty

claims.text: In 2014 Upworthy dropped pageviews for attention minutes, a blend of tab time, video time and mouse movement, and accepted lower traffic for it.
claims.quote: In 2014 Upworthy dropped pageviews for a blend of tab time, video time and mouse movement, and accepted lower traffic for it

claims.text: On a 1920 by 1080 screen, 120 people spent 57% of their viewing time above the fold and 74% in the first two screens.
claims.quote: 120 people spent 57% of their viewing time above the fold and 74% in the first two screens

value.unit: percent of viewing time above the fold, 120 people

claims.text: Across 190 studies and 18,573 readers, adults read non-fiction silently at 238 words a minute on average, most between 175 and 300.
claims.quote: adults read non-fiction silently at 238 words a minute on average, most between 175 and 300

value.unit: words a minute, average adult silent reading of non-fiction

claims.text: The W3C Web Annotation model anchors a highlight by its exact words and a little text either side, not by a position, so it survives changes elsewhere in the page.
claims.quote: The W3C Web Annotation model anchors a highlight by its exact words and a little of the text before and after (a text quote selector), not by a position

claims.text: The industry's measures are all the publisher's, sent to a server; the newsroom's have to live in the reader's browser and be the reader's.
claims.quote: The industry's measures are all the publisher's, sent to a server; ours have to live in the reader's browser and be the reader's.

claims.text: Scrolled is how much of each section has passed through the middle 70% of the window, and it only grows.
claims.quote: marks how far each section has passed through it: that is scrolled, and it only grows

claims.text: Read is the time a section was in the reading band while the tab was in front, focused and the reader active in the last 60 seconds; a section is read when its time reaches its words at 300 a minute.
claims.quote: A section is read when its time reaches its words at 300 a minute, the top of the normal range.

claims.text: The chip now shows scrolled, read and the page's cost, no balance, with every value in a fixed-width box with tabular figures, and only changed text written.
claims.quote: Every value sits in a box of fixed width with tabular figures, and only text that changed is written

claims.text: Tapping the chip opens the article as a map of its sections, with a pale bar for scrolled, a solid one for read, and the highlights in each.
claims.quote: Tap the chip and the article opens as a map: each section, a pale bar for scrolled and a solid one for read

claims.text: Highlights are one gesture, kept in the browser and drawn with the CSS Custom Highlight API, so the published article stays byte for byte what was published.
claims.quote: It is drawn with the CSS Custom Highlight API, so the published article stays byte for byte what was published

claims.text: In a hand test, opening an article and flicking to near the bottom gave 90% scrolled and 1% read.
claims.quote: Opened it, flicked to near the bottom | 90% | 1%

value.unit: percent read after a flick to near the bottom, against 90 percent scrolled

claims.text: The release sends nothing anywhere, the vault does not carry the records yet, and it does not change what the meter charges.
claims.quote: It sends nothing anywhere, and the vault does not carry it yet. It does not change what the meter charges.

claims.text: It cannot tell a reader looking at the screen from one who left the room with the pointer on the page; the 60 second rule is a guess, and figures and code are counted as words.
claims.quote: the 60 second rule is a guess, and a better one would come from the reader's own data.

claims.text: Should the meter charge for reading rather than for scrolling?
claims.quote: Should the meter charge for reading?

claims.text: Charge by scroll, settle by read: the meter charges as now and, when the reader leaves or rates, the charge settles to the larger of 10% and what was read.
claims.quote: Charge by scroll, settle by read. The meter charges as now, and when the reader leaves, or rates, the charge settles to the larger of 10% and what was read.

claims.text: The agent recommends the third option but not yet: first a fortnight of the owner's own reading in the new records, then a decision written down as the meter's rules are.
claims.quote: My recommendation is the third, but not yet. First, a fortnight of the owner's own reading in the new records

claims.text: A Links: more mode would turn the concepts other articles define, and the subjects they share, into links in the text, each with a card saying what the concept is and where else it appears.
claims.quote: the concepts the other articles define, and the subjects they share, become links in this one, each with a card that says what the concept is and where else it appears.

claims.text: On the tokens hook article the prototype adds 22 links to the 26 its author wrote, most of them from tags because so few concept labels are shared.
claims.quote: On the tokens hook article it adds 22 links to the 26 its author wrote.

value.unit: links added to the links the author wrote

claims.text: The work before the mode is worth turning on is a shared vocabulary of concepts, which is the Librarian's job.
claims.quote: The work is a shared vocabulary of concepts, which is the Librarian's job, before the mode is worth turning on.

claims.text: The account page would show one row per article: scrolled and read side by side, a verdict of read, part read, skimmed or started, and how many passages were highlighted, built from the browser's records.
claims.quote: On the account page, one row per article: how far you scrolled and how much you read, side by side, a verdict (read, part read, skimmed, started) and how many passages you highlighted.

claims.text: The three prototypes are pictures of real articles with real data, drawn into the page for the screenshot only; none of them is on the site.
claims.quote: These three are pictures of real articles with real data from the newsroom's own files, drawn into the page for the screenshot only.

claims.text: Articles written by an agent under its own name are now listed under Written by the agents, with the newest three in a block of their own on the front page, kept off the automatic lead.
claims.quote: they are listed at Written by the agents, with the agents' own pages, and the front page shows the newest three in a block of their own.

claims.text: The Librarian should merge the concept labels across the article graphs into a shared vocabulary, as the tags were merged into 42 subjects, and the findability file should carry them.
claims.quote: A shared vocabulary of concepts. The Librarian merges the concept labels across the article graphs, as the tags were merged into 42 subjects

claims.text: The reading store is one key, sgit.reading.v1, with one record per page and at most 400 pages, oldest dropped first.
claims.quote: One key, sgit.reading.v1, one record per page, at most 400 pages, oldest dropped first

value.unit: pages kept in the browser's reading store
